Q: Intermittent 403 Forbidden client error response status code when scraping with Selenium A:

The fact that it clears itself after 45-60 seconds points at a per-IP rate limit rather than bot detection. Fingerprint blocks don't expire on a timer; a token bucket refilling does exactly this. Same behaviour from your laptop and EC2 fits, since the counter is per source IP.

First, drop the user agent override. Chrome 60 is from 2017, but Sec-CH-UA and navigator.userAgentData still report your real modern build. That mismatch is a stronger automation signal than an honest UA would be.

Then add jitter instead of a flat sleep: time.sleep(random.uniform(1.5, 4)) between records, and exponential backoff on the 403 rather than a fixed 60.

If you still need more throughput, spread it over more IPs. Buy a handful of ISP proxies (static residential): datacenter-hosted but registered to a consumer ASN, so they're fast and stable while carrying residential reputation. Plain datacenter proxies are mostly pre-flagged and will make things worse.

The important bit with Selenium: don't rotate per request. If the IP changes mid-session while cookies and TLS state stay the same, that's more suspicious than the rate limiting you're escaping. One IP per browser session, rotate at session boundaries:

for chunk in chunks(records, size=200):
    opts = webdriver.ChromeOptions()
    opts.add_argument(f"--proxy-server=http://{next_proxy()}")
    driver = webdriver.Chrome(options=opts)
    try:
        for record in chunk:
            fetch(driver, record)
            time.sleep(random.uniform(1.5, 4)
    finally:
        driver.quit()

Five IPs gives you roughly five times the heata dir per session so cookies don't follow youacross IPs.

Also worth checking how you detect the 403, since Selenium doesn't expose status codes. If you're reading the rendered page, make sure a soft block (200 with a chalunted as success.

Q: HLSL TraceRay always return no intersection A:

I wasn't setting the instances instance mask when building the TLAS.
So this:

instanceDescs[i] = nvrhi::rt::InstanceDesc()
            .setBLAS(m_blases[i])
            .setFlags(nvrhi::rt::InstanceFlags::None)
            .setTransform(m_instanceTransforms[i])
            .setInstanceID(i);

Need to be changed to this:

instanceDescs[i] = nvrhi::rt::InstanceDesc()
                .setBLAS(m_blases[i])
                .setFlags(nvrhi::rt::InstanceFlags::None)
                .setTransform(m_instanceTransforms[i])
                .setInstanceID(i)
                .setInstanceMask(1);

Q: SSIS data migration from one db to other db A:

So, ok the issue you're experiencing is due to how SSIS handles data truncation by default within the OLE DB Destination. When your source data exceeds the destination column length, the component often performs an implicit truncation rather than raising an error, because the "Truncation" property for the columns is set to "Ignore Failure" in the Advanced Editor. Since the SSIS pipeline doesn't see this as a hard execution error, it simply clips the string to fit the destination column size and continues processing the row normally, preventing it from ever being redirected to your error output.

To fix this, you need to configure the OLE DB Destination to treat truncation as an error instead of ignoring it. Open the Advanced Editor for your destination, navigate to the Input and Output Properties tab, and expand the OLE DB Destination Input and then External Columns. Select the column that is being truncated, and in the properties pane, locate the TruncationRowDisposition setting and change it from RD_IgnoreFailure to RD_RedirectRow. Once you do this, the pipeline will recognize the length mismatch as a row-level error, and the SSIS error output will correctly catch and redirect those records to your log table.

Q: Your code displayed no output A: 
def readable_timedelta(days):

    """Print the number of weeks and days in a number of days."""
    
    # to get the number of weeks we use integer division
    weeks = days // 7
    
    # to get the number of days that remain we use %, the modulus operator
    remainder = days % 7
    
    return "{} week(s) and {} day(s)".format(weeks, remainder)


# Calling Function
print(readable_timedelta(20))
print(readable_timedelta(40))

Q: Subfile WRITE fails with CPF5021 (status 9N / extended status 831D), even on a minimal test program A:

Thanks for the tip on editing vs commenting, and for the suggestion! I actually found the root cause via a different path in the meantime: the indicator area needs to be declared as PIC 1 OCCURS 99 TIMES INDICATOR 1 (COBOL's native boolean type), not PIC X — using PIC X compiles fine and WRITE succeeds, but the READ specifically fails with CPF5022 regardless of indicator values. Also needed WRITE SUBFILE (not just WRITE) on the detail record format. Posting a full answer with the working code below.
